entities.summary: Arnoald, a bishop of Metz between 601 and 609 or 611, played a pivotal role in the ecclesiastical and political landscape of the Frankish kingdom during the 7th century. Born to a senatorial family, Arnoald succeeded his uncle Agilulf as bishop, inheriting a position of significant influence and authority within the Catholic Church. He was the son of Ansbertus and Blithilde, whose parents were Charibert I and Ingoberga. Through his leadership and strategic alliances, Arnoald contributed to the consolidation of Frankish power and the spread of Christianity throughout the region. His legacy extends beyond his own time, shaping the course of Western Christian history and influencing the development of the Church in the centuries that followed. As the son of a senator, Arnoald's background reflects the complex web of relationships between the nobility, the Church, and the emerging nation-state of the Frankish kingdom. His life serves as a testament to the interconnected nature of power, faith, and identity in the early Middle Ages.
